def count_valued_over_25(names, values):
    """Alright, picture the scene: it's card-show weekend and your buddy runs a
    folding table at the convention center, selling sports memorabilia —
    trading cards, signed pucks, game-worn wristbands, the whole spread. He
    keeps inventory the most old-school way imaginable: two parallel lists
    scribbled in a notebook, one holding the item names and the other holding
    what he figures each piece is worth in dollars. names is a list of strings
    and values is a list of ints of the same length; names[i] and values[i]
    describe the same item.

    Here's the thing. The show organizers have a house rule: the pricier stuff
    belongs in the locked display case up front — think of it as the premium
    seating behind home plate, reserved for the headliners. Before the doors
    open, your buddy wants a quick headcount of how many of his pieces make
    the cut, so he knows how much glass-case real estate to ask for. That's
    your whole assignment, and it's about as gentle as a warm-up lap. Count
    the items whose value is strictly greater than 25.

    That's it — no sorting the roster, no tallying dollar totals, no MVP
    voting. Just walk the lineup once and see how many items clear that bar,
    like a scout counting how many prospects can hit the fastball. Give back
    that single number and you can hit the showers early.

    Examples:
    >>> count_valued_over_25([], [])
    0
    >>> count_valued_over_25(['dyn', 'eel', 'bolt', 'fig', 'dyn', 'bolt', 'cam'], [9, 35, 4, 5, 14, 21, 31])
    2
    """
